newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods preserve gains on crude rally.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods preserve gains on crude rally.

text.p: U.S. spot liquids prices late Monday preserved their intraday gains as crude settled a boisterous 47 cents a barrel higher, players said, although afternoon dealings were described as paper thin.

Mont Belvieu propane remained offered at 35.75 cents a barrel, steady with midday but a half cent firmer than late last week, following a spree of buyer short covering earlier Monday as crude rallied.
Conway propane was sold for 36.0 cents a barrel, also 0.75 cent firmer than late Friday, helped as well by short covering.

"Buyers with shorts out are getting nervous as crude keeps climbing and are grabbing any propane that appears," one Conway player said, adding sellers seemed reluctant to part with barrels in hopes of even firmer future prices.
One Belvieu trader said many players unloaded large propane parcels several weeks ago when prices dipped below 36.0 cents a barrel, for fear prices would drop lower.
"They have been holding off buying but came back in today to cover their shorts. They didn't want to be caught later if crude keeps heading higher," he said.
Other liquids prices also benefitted from the crude rally, including Conway ethane mix, which was offered for 15.25 cents a gallon, one cent firmer than Friday, players said.
